other_failure_modes.name: DataLeakageInCV
other_failure_modes.description: Transformers such as TF-IDF and SVD are fitted on the entire training set before the cross-validation loop. This leaks information from the validation folds into the training folds, making the out-of-fold validation score overly optimistic.

other_failure_modes.name: HardcodedSubmissionId
other_failure_modes.description: The agent hardcodes the submission ID column with sequential integers instead of extracting the actual ID column from the test dataset. This will result in a failed submission if the test IDs are not 0-indexed sequential integers.

other_failure_modes.name: IDColumnAsFeature
other_failure_modes.description: The agent does not identify or drop identifier columns (like 'id' or 'ID') from the training data. Using IDs as features can lead to overfitting, and it further confirms that the hardcoded submission IDs will mismatch the expected format.

other_failure_modes.name: TargetEncodingWithoutSmoothing
other_failure_modes.description: The out-of-fold target encoding computes simple category means without any smoothing or regularization. This can lead to overfitting for rare categories.

summary: The agent implements a generally solid baseline using HistGradientBoosting, cross-validation, and extensive feature engineering including out-of-fold target encoding and text SVD. However, there are a few critical flaws: it fails to drop the dataset's ID column (treating it as a feature) and hardcodes the submission IDs, which will likely cause a submission failure. Additionally, it fits TF-IDF and SVD on the entire training set before CV, causing data leakage that will inflate the validation score.
